newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Srong Irish economy drives Jurys H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Srong Irish economy drives Jurys H1 profits.

text.p: Leading Irish hotel group Jurys on Thursday reported a 39 percent rise in half-year profits, helped by a buoyant Irish economy, another bumper year for Irish tourism and an improving British economy.

Pre-tax profits rose to 7.92 million Irish pounds ($13.1 million) while turnover at the hotel group, which derives around 75 percent of its trade from business customers with a further 25 percent coming from tourism, rose 17 percent to 29.3 million.
"The fruits of our development strategy which has broadened Jury's market appeal in Ireland and expanded our presence in the UK can be seen in these results," the group said in a statement.
"Market conditions in Ireland are buoyant, reflecting strong economic performance and our properties in the UK are well positioned to benefit from sustained recovery in that market."
Jurys has expanded into the British market in recent years, acquiring hotels in London, Cardiff, Bristol and Glasgow while developing its inn brand closer to home.
The inns, three-star hotels featuring moderately priced accomodation, are designed to complement Jurys' existing four and five-star hotels by broadening the scope of potential business for the group.
Jurys now has inns in Dublin, Cork and Galway and is planning to open a new inn in Belfast in early April followed by a Limerick inn at the end of April.

"The buildings are well on, the managers have been appointed, the staff are being trained and bookings are coming in. We are very optimistic about the Belfast and Limerick inns," managing director Peter Malone told a news conference.
The group also hopes to commence construction of a 168-bedroom Jurys Inn in London's Pentonville Road by April 1997 and would like to further extend the concept in Britain.
"We would like to go into other cities in Britain. We think the inns concept will travel," Malone said.
Jurys, which owned just three hotels in 1990, will be running 16 hotels in Britain and Ireland once the London inn is completed and is also keeping an eye out for opportunities in continental Europe.

"We are looking but not rushing. We would like to go to Northern Europe," Malone said, adding that with gearing at nine percent and plenty of committed bank lines, the group has the ability to move quickly if an opportunity arises.
Meanwhile, Jurys remains confident about the remainder of this financial year.
"Trading across the group for the initial months of the second half of our year has shown considerable improvement over the corresponding months of last year.
"Current indications are that the year ending April 30, 1997 will prove yet another record year," the company said.
Jurys share price was up five pence at 285 by 1346 GMT. ($ = 0.602 Irish Pounds)
